concepts.title: The Structure of the Atom
concepts.summary: Reconstructing the history of atomic models, from Dalton's solid spheres to Rutherford's nuclear atom and Bohr's quantized orbits.
concepts.history_text: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 using cathode ray tube experiments, proving atoms are divisible.

sections.content:
An atom consists of a dense, positively charged nucleus containing **protons** and **neutrons**, surrounded by a cloud of negatively charged **electrons**.

Key properties:
* Proton: charge = +1, mass $\approx 1\text{ amu}$
* Neutron: charge = 0, mass $\approx 1\text{ amu}$
* Electron: charge = -1, mass $\approx \frac{1}{1836}\text{ amu}$
If the nucleus of an atom contains only positive protons and neutral neutrons, why doesn't electrostatic repulsion blow the nucleus apart? What other fundamental force must be at play here?

**Isotopes** are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons (atomic number $Z$) but different numbers of neutrons (mass number $A$).

The relative atomic mass ($A_r$) of an element is the weighted average of the isotopic masses:
$$A_r = \sum (\text{abundance}_i \times \text{mass}_i)$$
Simulate mass spectrometry data by weighing small plastic beads of different colors representing isotopes. Calculate the weighted average mass of your bead 'element'.

concepts.title: Chemical Bonding
concepts.summary: Exploring how atoms share or transfer valence electrons to achieve stable octets, creating ionic, covalent, and metallic bonds.
concepts.history_text: Gilbert N. Lewis proposed the octet rule in 1916, introducing electron dot structures to represent valence shells.

sections.content:
**Ionic bonding** occurs when metal atoms transfer electrons to non-metal atoms, forming cations and anions held together by strong electrostatic attractions.

Example: $\text{Na} \to \text{Na}^+ + e^-$ and $\text{Cl} + e^- \to \text{Cl}^-$. The resulting $\text{NaCl}$ forms a giant ionic crystal lattice.
Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity when dissolved in water or melted, but are complete insulators in their solid crystal state?

**Covalent bonding** involves the sharing of valence electron pairs between non-metal atoms to achieve stable noble gas configurations.

Shared pairs can form single ($H-H$), double ($O=O$), or triple ($N\equiv N$) bonds, which vary in bond length and strength.
Use molecular model kits to construct 3D models of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{CO}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$. Draw Lewis structures for each showing shared pairs and lone pairs.

concepts.title: The Mole and Avogadro's Constant
concepts.summary: Bridging the microscopic scale of atoms with the macroscopic scale of laboratory measurements using the mole.
concepts.history_text: Amedeo Avogadro proposed in 1811 that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

sections.content:
One **mole** ($1\text{ mol}$) contains exactly $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ elementary particles (Avogadro's constant, $N_A$).

The relation between mass ($m$), molar mass ($M$), and moles ($n$) is:
$$n = \frac{m}{M}$$
If you have $18\text{ g}$ of water (exactly 1 mole of water molecules), how many hydrogen atoms do you have? Show your reasoning.
